ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Not an ultrasound-guided technique -- injected directly, via an intraoral/transoral needle approach into the tongue substance, under EMG guidance. Used as an adjunct in the protrusion type of lingual dystonia when the tongue shows flattening/widening that the genioglossus injection alone does not correct.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: EMG confirmation of recruitment during the dystonic flattening/widening movement.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Only described as one component of an individualized, EMG-mapped injection plan for lingual dystonia, not as a standalone BoNT indication -- vertical tongue is not a typical or independently-targeted BoNT muscle. Total lingual-muscle dose per session averaged ~43 U across whichever combination of muscles the EMG mapping indicated.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Yoshida K, 'Botulinum Neurotoxin Therapy for Lingual Dystonia Using an Individualized Injection Method Based on Clinical Features', Toxins (Basel) 11(1):51 (2019), doi:10.3390/toxins11010051 -- retrieved via PubMed.
